newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA PRESIDENT STILL BACKING ROBSON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA PRESIDENT STILL BACKING ROBSON.

text.p: Barcelona president Jose Luis Nunez has underlined his confidence in beleaguered coach Bobby Robson as the team face a home Spanish league clash against Zaragoza on Sunday.
Former England manager Robson was given backing by Nunez only hours before Barcelona suffered another away defeat -- 2-0 at Real Sociedad on Thursday.
"(Robson) hasn't got an ultimatum, and I want him to finish this and next season," said Nunez.

"My opinion continues to be that the valuation should be done at the end of the year. The misfortunes... have been blown out of all proportion ... It's very difficult to play badly and score more goals than anybody else."
Nunez also compared Robson's position with that of Fabio Capello, who had watched his Real Madrid side lose their unbeaten league record this season the previous day.
"Real Madrid lost and I haven't read any criticism of their coach," he said.

Real's defeat at Rayo Vallecano had opened the door to Barcelona to cut the gap at the top to just three points. But Robson's side squandered the opportunity against Sociedad, and went down to a dubious penalty and a fluke goal caused by an appalling defensive blunder.
Robson was visibly angered by the refereeing decisions, which he called "ridiculous".

The Barcelona-Zaragoza fixture traditionally produces classic games, and even more memorable scorelines. There were eight goals in a characteristically action-packed encounter between the two sides earlier this season.
That result left Barcelona on top of the first divison, but things have gone badly wrong at the Nou Camp since then, and most commentators believe Robson will not last the season.
Zaragoza, after slipping deep into the relegation zone, have shown signs of resurgence in recent weeks and once again look capable of producing a game worthy of the fixture's recent history.
